steps.intent: Algeria's objective, acting on behalf of the Arab Group and united with the ten elected members (E10), is to establish a clear, binding demand for an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire in Gaza, ensure unrestricted humanitarian access, protect UNRWA, and secure the unconditional release of all hostages. The central point of contention will be the United States' insistence on explicitly conditioning any ceasefire on the prior or concurrent release of hostages and its refusal to support a text that does not condemn Hamas. Balancing the urgent need to halt the destruction and starvation in Gaza with the constant threat of a US veto represents the most formidable diplomatic challenge during negotiations.

messages.China: China highly appreciates the leadership and untiring efforts of Algeria and all the elected members (E10) in drafting this clear, balanced, and principled resolution. The text rightly demands an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, which reflects the overwhelming consensus of the international community and is long overdue. We fully support this initiative and suggest reinforcing the draft by reaffirming the fundamental commitment to the two-State solution and explicitly rejecting forced displacement.
messages.Ecuador: As a co-sponsor and member of the E10, Ecuador fully supports this draft resolution, which addresses the urgent humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza and rightly demands both an immediate ceasefire and the unconditional release of all hostages. We believe adding a standard reaffirmation of the two-State solution would further strengthen the text and promote broader Council unity. We stand ready to work closely with Algeria and all E10 colleagues to bring this text across the finish line.
messages.France: France commends the ten elected members for this crucial and timely initiative, and we fully support the demand for an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire alongside the immediate release of all hostages. To ensure balance and reflect Council principles, we strongly urge the inclusion of a clear condemnation of the terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas on 7 October 2023, as well as a reaffirmation of the two-State political horizon. We will vote in favour of this text to alleviate the intolerable humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza.
messages.Guyana: Guyana fully supports this draft resolution, which we are proud to co-sponsor alongside the other elected members of the Council. The text appropriately reflects the urgent imperative of demanding an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, alongside the unconditional release of all hostages and unhindered humanitarian access throughout the Gaza Strip. In the face of catastrophic civilian suffering and famine, the Council must shoulder its Charter responsibilities and adopt this resolution without delay.
messages.Japan: As a co-sponsor of this E10 initiative, Japan fully supports the urgent imperative to halt the catastrophic humanitarian crisis in Gaza and secure the release of all hostages. To ensure broad Council consensus and foster balance, we strongly encourage incorporating an explicit condemnation of the 7 October terrorist attacks by Hamas. We also suggest reinforcing the vital link between an immediate ceasefire and the unconditional release of all hostages.
messages.Malta: As a proud co-sponsor of this collective E10 initiative, Malta fully supports the draft resolution as presented. The text reflects the critical imperatives we have consistently championed: an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and unhindered humanitarian access to avert famine. We urge all Council members to support this balanced and urgent text to uphold our Charter responsibilities.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique fully supports the draft resolution as formulated and stands firmly behind our collective E10 initiative. The text appropriately addresses the catastrophic humanitarian crisis by demanding an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire alongside the immediate release of all hostages and unhindered humanitarian access. We emphasize the importance of maintaining E10 unity to send an unequivocal message on the protection of civilians and respect for international humanitarian law.
messages.Republic of Korea: As a co-sponsor of this draft resolution alongside our fellow elected members, the Republic of Korea fully supports the text as presented. The draft strikes an essential balance by demanding an immediate and unconditional ceasefire while reiterating the urgent demand for the unconditional release of all hostages. In light of the deepening humanitarian catastrophe and famine risk in Gaza, the Council must demonstrate unity and act decisively to save civilian lives and ensure unhindered humanitarian access.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation fully supports the draft resolution prepared by the ten elected members of the Security Council. A direct, binding demand for an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, alongside unhindered humanitarian access and full support for UNRWA, is long overdue and essential to halt the catastrophic bloodshed in Gaza. We urge all Council members to maintain the integrity of this text and move swiftly to its adoption without further delay or watering down.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone stands firmly behind this draft resolution as a co-sponsor alongside our fellow E10 members. Given the catastrophic humanitarian crisis, impending famine, and continued loss of civilian life in Gaza, it is imperative that the Council speaks with one voice to demand an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, alongside the unconditional release of all hostages. We support preserving the integrity and strength of this agreed E10 text without dilution.
messages.Slovenia: As a proud co-sponsor of this draft alongside our fellow elected members, Slovenia fully supports the text as presented. It faithfully reflects the imperative for an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, the immediate release of all hostages, unhindered humanitarian aid delivery, and unequivocal support for UNRWA. We urge all Council members, particularly the permanent members, to rally behind this balanced and essential E10 initiative to alleviate civilian suffering.
messages.Switzerland: As a proud co-sponsor of this E10 initiative, Switzerland fully supports the draft's essential demands for an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire, the immediate release of all hostages, and unimpeded humanitarian access. Upholding international humanitarian law and protecting civilians remain our paramount priorities. To reinforce consistency with resolution 2735 (2024) and maintain a viable political horizon, we propose including a preambular paragraph reaffirming the Council's commitment to the two-State solution.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes the E10's leadership and the draft's focus on ending the catastrophic humanitarian suffering in Gaza, securing the release of hostages, and scaling up humanitarian assistance. To ensure broad Council unity and balance, we strongly urge the inclusion of an unequivocal condemnation of the 7 October terror attacks by Hamas, as well as clearer language linking the demand for a ceasefire with the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. We stand ready to engage constructively with the co-sponsors to achieve an agreed text that can be adopted.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot accept any draft that demands an unconditional ceasefire without inextricably linking it to the immediate release of all hostages held by Hamas. An unconditional cessation of hostilities would simply leave Hamas intact, in power, and able to repeat the horrors of October 7, while abandoning the hostages. Any product from this Council must uphold the framework of resolution 2735 (2024) and explicitly condemn Hamas's terrorism.

before.Algeria:
Mr. President,

I have the honour to speak on behalf of the ten elected members of the Security Council (E10): Ecuador, Guyana, Japan, Malta, Mozambique, the Republic of Korea, Sierra Leone, Slovenia, Switzerland, and my own country, Algeria.

For more than fourteen months, the Security Council has stood unable to halt the catastrophic violence and unfolding tragedy in Gaza. Over forty-four thousand Palestinians have been killed, the vast majority women and children, while tens of thousands more remain wounded, missing, or buried beneath the rubble. In northern Gaza, civilians are subjected to an unrelenting siege, facing imminent famine and systematic destruction.

Throughout extensive consultations over the past weeks, the E10 has worked tirelessly and in good faith to bridge differences and draft a balanced, action-oriented text that responds to the urgency on the ground. The draft resolution before us today is clear: it demands an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire to be respected by all parties, and reiterates the demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. It also demands unhindered humanitarian access and rejects any attempt to starve Palestinians, while upholding the indispensable role of UNRWA.

This text represents the collective will of the elected members and the overwhelming consensus of the international community. It is time for this Council to fulfill its Charter mandate, protect innocent lives, and put an end to this nightmare. We urge all members to vote in favour of this draft resolution.

Thank you.

after.Algeria:
Mr. President,

I speak now in my national capacity.

Today is a sad day—a sad day for the Security Council, for the United Nations, and for the international community as a whole. 

For the fourth time since the start of the aggression against Gaza, this Council has been prevented from shouldering its primary responsibility under the Charter to maintain international peace and security and to put an end to the ongoing slaughter of innocent Palestinian civilians. 

Fourteen members of this Council stood together today in favour of a text that demanded an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, the release of all hostages, and the unhindered flow of humanitarian assistance to people facing imminent famine. The ten elected members worked diligently, constructively, and in good faith for weeks, accommodating concerns and making substantial compromises to achieve a meaningful consensus. Yet once again, a single veto has paralyzed our collective action.

Today’s message is devastating. To the occupying Power, it sends a message of continued impunity—a license to proceed with the extermination and starvation of the Palestinian people, to pursue the systematic destruction of northern Gaza, and to remain above international law. 

To the Palestinian people, who have endured over fourteen months of unprecedented agony, displacement, and loss, today’s outcome is a cruel disappointment. But we want them to know that they are not alone. Fourteen members of this Council—representing the overwhelming majority of humanity—voted to end this nightmare. 

Algeria, alongside all nations of conscience, will never give up. We will not tire, and we will not surrender to paralysis. Just as we have promised before, we will return to knock on the doors of this Council again and again until the Security Council finally assumes its duties, brings an end to this barbaric aggression, and ensures that the Palestinian people realize their inalienable right to self-determination and freedom in their independent State.

I thank you.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the ten elected members of the Security Council. We express our deep disappointment at the outcome of the vote. The exercise of the veto by the United States once again has shattered the hopes of the people of Gaza for survival and pushed them further into darkness and despair.

More than 44,000 people have lost their lives in Gaza, and the humanitarian disaster there has reached unprecedented proportions. In northern Gaza, hundreds of thousands of civilians are suffering under a brutal siege, facing imminent famine, deprivation of basic necessities, and continuous bombardment. When will this tragedy end? How many more innocent lives must be lost before the guns are silenced?

The draft resolution put forward by the ten elected members was balanced, reasonable, and fully reflected the overwhelming consensus of the international community. It demanded an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, and called for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. It also stressed the vital and irreplaceable role of UNRWA and the urgent need to ensure humanitarian access at scale. The draft fully demonstrated the sincerity and constructive approach of the E10, for which we express our sincere appreciation.

Yet, one permanent member once again single-handedly blocked the Security Council from fulfilling its primary responsibility under the UN Charter. Every time the United States has used its veto to shield Israel, it has pushed the situation deeper into catastrophe. The continuous use of the veto has reduced Council authority and international law to mere rhetoric. People cannot help but ask: Do Palestinian lives not matter? Is the death of tens of thousands of women and children just collateral damage?

The Council must not allow the collective punishment of the Palestinian people to continue. We demand that Israel immediately cease its military operations in Gaza, lift the blockade, halt the forced displacement of civilians, and stop the weaponization of food and humanitarian supplies. We reiterate our firm support for UNRWA, which is the lifeline for millions of Palestinian refugees.

The Palestinian question lies at the heart of the Middle East issue. The only viable path to lasting peace is the full implementation of the two-State solution and the restoration of the legitimate national rights of the Palestinian people. China will continue to work tirelessly with the international community to uphold justice, end the conflict, alleviate the humanitarian disaster, and achieve a comprehensive, just, and lasting settlement of the question of Palestine.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France deeply regrets that the Security Council was unable to adopt the draft resolution submitted by the ten elected members, for which we voted.

The humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip is catastrophic and continues to worsen each day. The risk of famine, particularly in northern Gaza, is acute and unacceptable. Given this emergency, the draft resolution rightly demanded an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, as well as the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. France does not forget its two nationals still being held hostage in Gaza, and we will continue our relentless efforts until all hostages are freed and reunited with their loved ones.

International humanitarian law must be respected by all, in all circumstances. France firmly rejects any use of starvation as a weapon of war and any attempt at forced displacement or demographic change in the Gaza Strip. Full, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access must be granted immediately across the entire territory, through all crossing points. In this regard, France reiterates its steadfast support for the United Nations and its agencies, particularly UNRWA, which plays an irreplaceable and vital role on the ground.

Finally, only a political solution can bring a lasting end to the suffering of both Israelis and Palestinians and ensure long-term stability in the region. France remains firmly committed to the two-State solution, with two democratic States living side by side in peace and security, within secure and recognized borders, with Jerusalem as the capital of both States. 

The Security Council must not remain silent. France will continue to shoulder its responsibilities and engage with all members to achieve a ceasefire, the release of all hostages, and the revival of a credible political horizon.

Thank you.
after.Guyana:
Mr. President,

Guyana voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted today by the ten elected members of the Security Council, and we express our profound regret and disappointment that, once again, this Council has been prevented from fulfilling its primary responsibility under the United Nations Charter due to the exercise of the veto.

For more than fourteen months, the world has witnessed an unrelenting catastrophe in the Gaza Strip. More than 44,000 Palestinians have been killed, the vast majority of them women and children, and tens of thousands more remain injured, missing, or buried beneath the rubble. Gaza has been reduced to an abyss of destruction and human suffering. In northern Gaza, civilians are enduring a brutal siege, trapped without access to food, water, or medicine, facing the imminent and terrifying reality of human-made famine.

The draft resolution put forward by the E10 was a balanced, necessary, and urgent response to this nightmare. It demanded what has long been overdue: an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, coupled with the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. It also demanded the immediate, unimpeded delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance at scale throughout the Gaza Strip and the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, in full compliance with international humanitarian law.

Guyana underscores that international humanitarian law is not optional. The starvation of civilians as a method of warfare is strictly prohibited, and the forced displacement of civilians is unlawful. We also reiterate our firm support for the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA), which remains the indispensable backbone of the humanitarian response in Gaza, and whose mandate must be protected and enabled.

Mr. President, a ceasefire is the only way to stop this devastation, to save the remaining hostages, to halt the descent into famine, and to create the conditions for a lasting peace. The failure to adopt this resolution today sends a devastating message to the millions of civilians who look to this Council for protection.

Guyana remains steadfast in its conviction that the only viable path to durable peace and security for both Palestinians and Israelis is the realization of the two-State solution, based on the pre-1967 borders, with two democratic States living side by side in peace and security. We will continue to support all efforts to end this war and bring relief to all affected civilians.

I thank you.
after.Japan:
Mr. President,

Japan deeply regrets that the Security Council was once again unable to adopt a draft resolution today, despite the earnest and tireless efforts of the ten elected members.

As a co-sponsor, Japan voted in favour of the draft resolution. For over thirteen months, the people of Gaza have endured unimaginable suffering. The humanitarian situation on the ground is beyond catastrophic, with the acute risk of famine looming, particularly in northern Gaza. Civilians, including women and children, are facing unbearable conditions without access to basic necessities for survival. International humanitarian law must be strictly respected by all parties under all circumstances.

At the same time, we cannot forget the hostages who have been held in Gaza by Hamas and other groups for more than four hundred days under appalling conditions. Japan unequivocally condemns the horrific terrorist attacks by Hamas and other militant groups on 7 October 2023. We reiterate our demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages.

Japan believes that an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire is essential to protect innocent civilian lives, create an environment conducive to the massive and unhindered delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance, and secure the release of all hostages. 

We also reiterate that UNRWA remains the backbone of the humanitarian response in Gaza. Its activities are indispensable, and its mandate must be enabled and respected.

Mr. President,

Japan remains deeply appreciative of the continued diplomatic efforts led by the United States, Egypt, and Qatar. The Council must not give up on its primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security. Japan reaffirms its unwavering commitment to a two-State solution, where Israel and an independent Palestinian State live side by side in peace and security. We will continue our diplomatic efforts and support to achieve lasting peace and stability in the region.

I thank you.
after.Malta:
Malta deeply regrets that the Security Council has once again failed to shoulder its primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security, owing to the use of a veto. 

Malta voted in favour of the draft resolution, which was painstakingly negotiated and presented by the ten elected members of this Council. The E10 showed true leadership, responsibility, and unity in putting forward a balanced and pragmatic text that sought to respond to the catastrophic reality on the ground in Gaza. 

For more than fourteen months, we have witnessed an unimaginable human tragedy. The situation in Gaza has reached unprecedented depths of despair, with northern Gaza enduring a suffocating siege and facing the imminent risk of famine. The sheer scale of death, destruction, and civilian suffering—most acutely felt by women and children—is utterly unacceptable. 

Malta has consistently demanded an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages held by Hamas and other groups, and the immediate, safe, and unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance at scale throughout the entire Gaza Strip. These demands are not mutually exclusive; they are mutually reinforcing and vital to saving human lives. 

We also reiterate our unwavering support for the United Nations, its agencies, and in particular UNRWA, which remains the irreplaceable backbone of the humanitarian response in Gaza. Any attempts to dismantle or obstruct its mandate will only deepen the catastrophe.

Compliance with international law, including international humanitarian law and international human rights law, is non-negotiable. Starvation of civilians as a method of warfare and the unlawful forced displacement of populations are strictly prohibited. 

Today’s failure cannot be the end of our efforts. The Council cannot remain paralyzed while millions face starvation, displacement, and death. Malta will continue to work tirelessly with all Council members and partners to bring an end to this conflict, to secure the release of all hostages, to alleviate humanitarian suffering, and to revive a political horizon towards a two-State solution where Israelis and Palestinians can live side by side in peace and security.

I thank you.
after.Republic of Korea:
Mr. President,

The Republic of Korea voted in favour of the draft resolution today as an elected member of the Security Council and one of its co-sponsors. We deeply regret that the Council was once again unable to adopt this resolution due to the veto of a permanent member.

More than thirteen months into this conflict, the humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip has reached unimaginable, catastrophic proportions. The impending risk of famine, particularly in northern Gaza, the near-total collapse of the healthcare system, and the continuous displacement and suffering of innocent civilians, especially women and children, demand our urgent and united action. International humanitarian law must be respected by all parties under all circumstances, and humanitarian aid must be allowed to enter Gaza safely, unhindered, and at scale. In this regard, we reaffirm that UNRWA remains the backbone of the humanitarian response and must be enabled to carry out its mandate.

At the same time, we reiterate our categorical condemnation of the horrific terrorist attacks led by Hamas on 7 October 2023, as well as the ongoing, inhumane holding of hostages. An immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire and the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages are desperately needed and inextricably linked to ending the unbearable suffering of both Palestinians and Israelis.

While today’s draft was not adopted, the Security Council cannot afford to give up on its primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security. The Republic of Korea urges all parties to fully implement resolution 2735 without further delay and calls for renewed diplomatic efforts to bring an end to the hostilities. Ultimately, the only viable path to durable peace and security for both Israelis and Palestinians lies in the realization of the two-State solution.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

Today we have witnessed another cynical and inhumane veto cast by the United States of America. By standing alone against the collective will of the overwhelming majority of the members of the Security Council and the entire international community, Washington has once again demonstrated its true priorities. 

Fourteen members of the Council voted today in support of a clear, unambiguous demand: an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire, the release of all hostages, and unimpeded humanitarian access to save millions of people on the brink of starvation. Yet the United States chose to block this modest and long-overdue step, effectively giving a green light to the continued slaughter and destruction in Gaza.

For more than fourteen months, we have heard endless lectures from our American colleagues about their so-called "quiet diplomacy" and claims that a deal is just around the corner. Time and again, the Council was told that any action on our part would disrupt sensitive negotiations. In June, the Council was pushed into adopting resolution 2735 (2024), which was presented as a viable roadmap backed by Israel. We warned back then that this was nothing more than an illusion, a smokescreen behind which West Jerusalem could continue its brutal military operation with complete impunity. Today’s veto confirms that the United States never intended to hold its ally accountable or to halt the bloodshed.

What is happening in Gaza is a catastrophe of unprecedented proportions. Over forty-four thousand Palestinians have been killed, the vast majority of them innocent women and children. Entire families have been wiped out, civilian infrastructure has been obliterated, and in northern Gaza, a deliberate campaign of starvation and forced displacement is underway before the eyes of the entire world. 

By vetoing this draft resolution, prepared with immense dedication and patience by the ten elected members, the United States bears full responsibility for every life that will be lost in the coming days and weeks. It is shameful that the Council remains paralyzed because one delegation places its domestic political interests and geopolitical ambitions above basic human decency and the lives of millions.

The Russian Federation will continue to stand firmly on the side of justice, international law, and the legitimate aspirations of the Palestinian people. The Security Council cannot abandon its responsibility under the United Nations Charter. We must demand an end to this madness, an end to the siege, and a genuine path toward a comprehensive, lasting settlement based on the recognized two-State formula.

Thank you.
after.Sierra Leone:
Mr. President,

Sierra Leone voted in favour of the draft resolution just considered, which was co-sponsored and presented by all ten elected members of the Security Council (E10). We express our deep regret and disappointment that, despite the overwhelming support of 14 Council members, the draft resolution was not adopted due to the exercise of the veto.

For more than fourteen months, the world has witnessed an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe in the Gaza Strip. More than 44,000 Palestinians, the overwhelming majority of them women and children, have been killed, with tens of thousands more injured, displaced, or trapped beneath the rubble. In northern Gaza, civilians endure a brutal siege, facing acute shortages of food, water, and medical care, and the imminent risk of famine. 

In the face of this profound human tragedy, the Security Council faced a clear political, legal, and moral imperative to act. As a proud member of the E10, Sierra Leone engaged constructively and in good faith throughout the drafting process to produce a balanced, principled text aimed at saving lives and upholding international law. 

The draft resolution clearly demanded an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire to be respected by all parties, while reiterating the demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. It also demanded the immediate, safe, and unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance at scale throughout Gaza, rejecting the starvation of civilians as a method of warfare, and underlined the indispensable and irreplaceable role of UNRWA as the backbone of the humanitarian response.

Mr. President,

The Security Council bears the primary responsibility under the Charter of the United Nations for the maintenance of international peace and security. Our repeated inability to act decisively to end the bloodshed, halt the collective punishment, and secure the release of hostages severely damages the credibility and authority of this Council and the collective security scheme of the United Nations. 

The killing must stop. The suffering must end. Sierra Leone reiterates that there can be no military solution to this conflict. We reaffirm our unwavering commitment to the two-State solution, where two democratic States, Israel and Palestine, live side by side in peace and security within secure and recognized borders, consistent with international law and relevant United Nations resolutions. 

Despite today’s setback, Sierra Leone remains committed to working with all Council members and international partners to achieve an immediate and lasting ceasefire, secure the unconditional release of all hostages, ensure the massive delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance, and advance a credible path toward lasting peace.

I thank you.
after.Switzerland:
Mr. President,

Switzerland deeply regrets that the Security Council was once again unable to adopt a resolution today to address the catastrophic situation in the Gaza Strip, owing to the use of the veto. 

As an elected member and co-sponsor of this draft resolution alongside the other nine elected members, Switzerland worked tirelessly and in good faith to reach a balanced text that reflected the urgent priorities of the Council and the international community. 

More than thirteen months into this war, the civilian suffering in Gaza has reached unimaginable proportions. In northern Gaza in particular, civilians are facing an acute risk of famine, enduring continuous bombardment and displacement, and deprived of the most basic necessities of life. This unbearable tragedy must come to an end.

Switzerland voted in favour of this draft resolution because its demands are vital and cannot be postponed. First, an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire to be respected by all parties is urgently required to stop the loss of human life and prevent further regional escalation. 

Second, this draft resolution unequivocally reiterated the demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages held by Hamas and other armed groups since the heinous terrorist acts of 7 October, which Switzerland has repeatedly condemned. Hostage-taking is a grave breach of international humanitarian law.

Third, the humanitarian situation demands immediate, safe, rapid, and unhindered humanitarian access throughout the Gaza Strip at scale. International humanitarian law is clear and non-negotiable: the starvation of civilians as a method of warfare is strictly prohibited. Civilians, medical personnel, and humanitarian workers must be respected and protected under all circumstances. In this context, Switzerland reiterates its full support for the United Nations, and in particular UNRWA, which remains the irreplaceable backbone of the humanitarian response in Gaza.

As the depositary of the Geneva Conventions, Switzerland recalls that all parties have an obligation to respect and ensure respect for international humanitarian law in all circumstances.

Finally, today's failure to act must not deter us from working towards a political horizon. Only a negotiated two-State solution, where two democratic States, Israel and Palestine, live side by side in peace and security within secure and recognized borders, can provide a lasting peace for Israelis and Palestinians alike. Switzerland will continue to work tirelessly to uphold the Charter of the United Nations, international law, and the Council’s responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security.

Thank you.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom voted in favour of this resolution. We did so because the situation in Gaza is catastrophic, and the suffering of civilians has gone on for far too long.

More than 400 days since the horrific terrorist attacks of 7 October, the nightmare in Gaza continues. In northern Gaza, famine is now imminent. Civilians are enduring unbearable conditions, with acute shortages of food, water, medical supplies, and shelter. An immediate ceasefire is desperately needed to halt the destruction, to allow a massive and unhindered surge in humanitarian assistance, and to secure the immediate and unconditional release of all remaining hostages held by Hamas.

The United Kingdom regrets that the Security Council was unable to speak with one voice today and reach agreement on this resolution. We also regret that the draft text did not contain an explicit condemnation of the barbaric terrorist atrocities committed by Hamas on 7 October 2023. Our position on Hamas’s terror is well known and remains unequivocal.

However, our vote today reflects our deep conviction that the Council had to act. The link between an immediate ceasefire, the release of all hostages, and the scaling up of aid is essential. International humanitarian law must be respected by all parties, civilians and humanitarian workers must be protected, and Israel must urgently lift all restrictions on aid delivery across the entirety of Gaza. Furthermore, we reiterate our support for UNRWA as the indispensable backbone of the humanitarian response.

Ultimately, there is no military solution to this conflict. We must urgently see an end to the fighting, the return of the hostages to their families, and renewed diplomatic momentum toward a viable political horizon: an irreversible pathway to a two-State solution, with a sovereign and viable Palestinian State living alongside a safe and secure Israel.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President.

We made it clear throughout negotiations that we could not support an unconditional ceasefire that fails to release the hostages. Because, as this Council has previously called for, a durable end to the war must come with the release of the hostages. These two urgent goals are inextricably linked. This resolution abandoned that necessity, and for that reason, the United States could not support it.

The resolution’s sponsors rejected efforts to forge a compromise, including language that would have made clear that a ceasefire must be linked to the release of hostages. A cessation of hostilities without the release of hostages is not a pathway to peace; it is a recipe for more conflict. It would leave Hamas in power in Gaza, able to regroup, rearm, and repeat the atrocities of October 7 again and again, just as its leaders have repeatedly promised to do. It would abandon the remaining hostages—including seven American citizens—still suffering in the brutal custody of a terrorist group.

Simply put, this text would have sent a dangerous message to Hamas: that there is no need to come back to the negotiating table, that it can hold onto hostages and wait for the international community to pressure Israel to walk away. We cannot allow that. It is Hamas that has repeatedly refused to negotiate in good faith, rejecting deal after deal, including proposals endorsed by this Council in resolution 2735.

Furthermore, we deeply regret that this Council, more than thirteen months after the horrific terrorist attacks of October 7, has once again failed to condemn Hamas. It is incomprehensible that some members of this Council continue to refuse to name and condemn the perpetrators of the worst massacre of Jews since the Holocaust.

The United States remains steadfastly committed to bringing an end to this conflict, securing the release of all hostages, surging humanitarian aid to civilians in Gaza, and charting a pathway toward a two-State solution. We have engaged in tireless diplomacy alongside Qatar and Egypt to achieve a ceasefire deal that brings the hostages home. That remains the only viable path to truly alleviate the catastrophic humanitarian suffering of Palestinian civilians and bring lasting security to the region.

We will continue to pursue real diplomacy on the ground, but we will not support Council action that undermines those efforts and rewards Hamas terrorism.

Thank you, Mr. President.
